Employee Health Analytics Dashboard

Business question: What are the main health risks in our workforce, and which departments, conditions and states need attention?

What the analysis found

  • Only 24% of the 300 employees are fully vaccinated; 76% are unvaccinated, partially vaccinated or unrecorded, which leaves the workforce exposed to avoidable infection risk.
  • 26% of employees are high risk and 64% are medium risk, the only group whose average sick days rose (from 10 to 11).
  • HR and Legal recorded the highest average sick days per employee (about 11 each in 2024), which may point to workload pressure.
  • Operations had the lowest mental health score (4.88/10) yet very low sick leave, a pattern consistent with presenteeism.
  • Hypertension was the most common chronic condition, affecting 22% of employees, and Rivers carried the highest health burden by state.

Recommendations

  • Run workplace vaccination drives backed by employee education.
  • Review workload and wellbeing support for HR, Legal and medium-risk staff, and assess Operations for presenteeism.
  • Introduce hypertension screening and preventive health education.

Hospital Clinical Insights Dashboard

Business question: Which patients use our hospitals most, which conditions and hospitals drive billing, how has patient volume changed, and how common are abnormal test results?

What the analysis found

  • Across 55,000+ records covering 18,069 unique patients, utilisation is concentrated in the older age groups for both men and women.
  • Diabetes accounts for the largest share of the £460.9M in total billing (16.8%), but spend is spread fairly evenly across conditions.
  • Billing is highly decentralised: the top 10 hospitals contribute just 2.8% of the total.
  • Patient volume rose around 2020 and fell in 2024, which may reflect changes in utilisation or in reporting.
  • 34% of test results were abnormal, a sizeable share that needs clinical follow-up.

Recommendations

  • Prioritise geriatric-focused care and chronic disease management, especially diabetes.
  • Standardise care pathways and cost tracking across facilities to improve visibility of spend.
  • Investigate the 2024 decline and follow up abnormal results with targeted checks.

Nigeria Disease Surveillance Dashboard

Business question: Where and when are disease cases occurring, who is most affected, which disease dominates, and what are the outcomes?

Simulated dataset created for portfolio purposes, not official surveillance data.

What the analysis found

  • Of 561 reported cases across 10 states, Lagos recorded the most (67, 11.9%) and Plateau the fewest (41, 7.3%), a fairly even geographic spread.
  • Cases rose 20% from Q3 (60) to Q4 (72) in 2025, after running below 2024 levels from Q1 to Q3.
  • Children aged 0–10 were the most affected group, followed by adults aged 81 and above.
  • Cholera was the most frequently reported disease.
  • 50.1% of cases recovered and 13.7% ended in death (77 deaths over 2024 and 2025), with Kaduna recording the most of any state (12).

Recommendations

  • Target children and older adults with age-specific interventions.
  • Strengthen cholera prevention through safe water, sanitation and early detection.
  • Investigate the Q4 rise and improve reporting completeness.

Maternal Health Analysis with SQL

Business question: Which regions and states carry the heaviest burden of maternal, neonatal and TB deaths, when did reported cases peak, and what is driving deaths in each state?

Data note: The dataset contains approximately 300 aggregated records, each representing reported mortality counts by state, year, and health indicator. SQL totals combine these counts across multiple records and indicators, so they may exceed the number of records.

What the analysis found

  • Across approximately 300 aggregated records covering nine states, the South West carried the heaviest burden with 53,639 reported deaths, roughly double the South East, which had the fewest at 26,631.
  • Reported cases peaked in 2023 at 42,229, the highest of any year in the data.
  • TB was the leading cause of death in 8 of the 9 states, ahead of maternal and neonatal deaths.

Recommendations

  • Focus maternal health and TB resources on the South West, where the reported burden is greatest.
  • Make TB control a core priority across 8 of 9 states, through screening, early treatment and follow-up.
  • Look into what drove the 2023 peak, whether a real rise or better reporting, before planning around it.

Childhood Vaccination Analysis with SQL

Business question: Which vaccines are children receiving most, how has uptake changed over the years, and which states are vaccinating the most?

What the analysis found

  • Of 300 children vaccinated across 5 vaccine types, Pentavalent was the most administered, with 66 vaccinations.
  • Uptake grew steadily from a single recorded vaccination in 2017 to a peak of 86 in 2023.
  • Vaccinations fell to 38 in 2024, down from the 2023 peak of 86.
  • Lagos recorded the most vaccinations (140) and Rivers the fewest (10), a 14-fold gap between states.

Recommendations

  • Investigate the 2024 decline (38 vaccinations, down from 86 in 2023) to find out whether it reflects gaps in access, supply or reporting.
  • Find out why Rivers lags behind Lagos, and direct outreach and supply to lower-performing states.
  • Compare uptake of the other four vaccines against Pentavalent to spot gaps in outreach.
